questions.stem: What is the formula for the area of a rectangle?
questions.explanation: Length times width gives area. Twice the sum gives perimeter instead.

questions.stem: What is the area of a rectangle 8 cm long and 5 cm wide?
questions.explanation: 8 × 5 = 40. The answer 26 is the perimeter.

questions.stem: What is the formula for the area of a triangle?
questions.explanation: A triangle is half the rectangle that encloses it, hence the half.

questions.stem: What is the area of a triangle with base 10 cm and height 6 cm?
questions.explanation: Half of 10 × 6 = half of 60 = 30. Forgetting the half gives 60.

questions.stem: What is the formula for the area of a parallelogram?
questions.explanation: It uses the perpendicular height, not the sloping side.

questions.stem: What is the sum of the interior angles of a triangle?
questions.explanation: Every plane triangle's interior angles total 180 degrees. 360 is the total for a quadrilateral.

questions.stem: What is the sum of the interior angles of a quadrilateral?
questions.explanation: A quadrilateral splits into two triangles, so 2 × 180 = 360.

questions.stem: What is the approximate value of pi?
questions.explanation: Pi is about 3.14159. It is the ratio of a circle's circumference to its diameter.
questions.teaching:
Pi is the ratio of a circle's circumference to its diameter, and it is the same for every circle no matter what size.

That constancy is what makes it useful: measure around any circular object and across it, divide one by the other, and you get the same number every time. It is irrational, so its decimal never ends or repeats, which is why calculations use a rounded value — two decimal places is standard at school, and the fraction 22/7 is a common alternative. Answers are often left in terms of the symbol itself, which is exact rather than rounded.

questions.stem: What does pi represent for a circle?
options: The area divided by the radius
The diameter divided by the radius
The circumference divided by the diameter
questions.explanation: Pi is that ratio, and it is the same for every circle. Diameter divided by radius is always exactly 2.

questions.stem: If a circle has radius 5 cm, what is its diameter?
questions.explanation: The diameter runs right across the circle through the centre, so it is twice the radius. Halving instead of doubling gives the radius back.

questions.stem: What is the formula for the circumference of a circle?
questions.explanation: C = pi × d, equivalently 2 × pi × r. Pi times radius squared gives area.

questions.stem: What is the volume of a rectangular prism 2 cm by 3 cm by 4 cm?
questions.explanation: Multiply all three dimensions: 2 × 3 × 4 = 24.

questions.stem: What unit is used for volume?
questions.explanation: Volume is three-dimensional, so units are cubed. Square units measure area.

questions.stem: What is a right angle?
questions.explanation: A right angle is a quarter turn. 180 degrees is a straight angle.

questions.stem: What are angles on a straight line called and what do they add to?
questions.explanation: Supplementary angles total 180. Complementary ones total 90.

questions.stem: What are vertically opposite angles?
options: Angles opposite each other where two lines cross, which are equal
Angles on the same side of a transversal
questions.explanation: When two straight lines cross, opposite angles are always equal.

questions.stem: What is the perpendicular height of a triangle?
options: The distance from the base to the opposite vertex at right angles
The length of the longest side
questions.explanation: It must be measured at right angles to the base, which is why it can fall outside the triangle.

questions.stem: What is a right prism?
options: A solid with all faces square
A solid with a curved surface
A solid with the same cross-section along its length and ends at right angles
Any solid with a triangular face
questions.explanation: A uniform cross-section is what allows volume = cross-sectional area × length.

questions.stem: How many degrees are in a full turn?
questions.explanation: A full revolution is 360 degrees.
questions.teaching:
Angle facts build on one another, so it is worth anchoring them to a complete rotation and working down.

A complete rotation is divided into 360 parts, a number inherited from Babylonian astronomy and convenient because it divides evenly so many ways. Half of that is a straight line, and a quarter is a right angle. From those three you can derive most of what you need: angles on a straight line sum to the half-turn figure, angles round a point sum to the full one, and a triangle's angles sum to the half-turn figure too. Confusing the straight-line value with the full rotation is the usual error.

questions.stem: What is the area of a square with side 7 cm?
questions.explanation: 7 × 7 = 49. The answer 28 is the perimeter.

questions.stem: Two parallel lines are crossed by a transversal. What is true of corresponding angles?
questions.explanation: Corresponding angles are equal when the lines are parallel. Co-interior angles are the pair that add to 180.

questions.stem: Two parallel lines are crossed by a transversal. What is true of co-interior angles?
questions.explanation: Co-interior (allied) angles are supplementary. Alternate and corresponding angles are the equal pairs.

questions.stem: A triangle has angles of 50 and 60 degrees. What is the third angle?
questions.explanation: A triangle's angles always total 180 degrees, so subtract both known angles: 180 - 50 - 60 = 70.

questions.stem: What is the volume of a triangular prism with cross-sectional area 12 cm^2 and length 10 cm?
questions.explanation: Volume of a right prism is cross-sectional area times length.

questions.stem: A circle has diameter 14 cm. Estimate its circumference using pi = 22/7.
questions.explanation: 22/7 × 14 = 44. The value 154 would be the area.

questions.stem: The area of a parallelogram is 48 cm^2 and its base is 8 cm. What is its perpendicular height?
questions.explanation: Rearranging area = base × height gives height = 48 ÷ 8 = 6.

questions.stem: Why does the area formula for a parallelogram use perpendicular height rather than the sloping side?
options: The two measurements are always equal
The perpendicular height gives the true vertical distance between the parallel sides
The sloping side is always shorter
questions.explanation: Using the slant side would overstate the area, because it is longer than the true separation of the parallel sides.

questions.stem: A rectangle's length is doubled while its width stays the same. What happens to its area?
questions.explanation: Area depends directly on length, so doubling one dimension doubles the area.

questions.stem: A square's side length is doubled. What happens to its area?
options: It becomes four times as large
It becomes eight times as large
questions.explanation: Both dimensions double, so the area scales by 2 × 2 = 4. Volume would scale by 8.

questions.stem: The interior angles of a pentagon add to how many degrees?
questions.explanation: A pentagon splits into three triangles, so 3 × 180 = 540.

questions.stem: A triangle has a base of 12 cm and area 42 cm^2. What is its perpendicular height?
questions.explanation: Area = half base × height, so 42 = 6 × height, giving height = 7.

questions.stem: Two similar rectangles have lengths in the ratio 1 : 3. What is the ratio of their areas?
questions.explanation: Area scales with the square of the length ratio, so 1 : 3 becomes 1 : 9.

questions.stem: Two similar solids have lengths in the ratio 1 : 2. What is the ratio of their volumes?
questions.explanation: Volume scales with the cube of the length ratio: 2^3 = 8.

questions.stem: Why is pi the same value for every circle?
options: It only holds for large circles
It is a coincidence of measurement
All circles are the same shape, so circumference and diameter scale together
Pi was defined by measuring one particular circle
questions.explanation: All circles are similar figures, so the ratio of any two corresponding lengths is constant.

questions.stem: A cube has volume 64 cm^3. What is the length of one edge?
questions.explanation: The edge is the cube root of the volume, and 4 × 4 × 4 = 64.

questions.stem: Why do angle facts about parallel lines fail if the lines are not parallel?
options: The equal and supplementary relationships depend on the lines never converging
The transversal meets each line at a different point
questions.explanation: Parallelism is the condition for those relationships. Without it, corresponding angles simply differ.

questions.stem: A rectangular tank measures 50 cm by 30 cm by 20 cm. How many litres does it hold?
questions.explanation: Volume is 30 000 cm^3, and 1 litre is 1000 cm^3, so it holds 30 litres.

questions.stem: Which explains why a triangle's angles always total 180 degrees?
options: Drawing a line parallel to one side creates angles that together form a straight line
It follows from the fact that a circle has 360 degrees
It is a definition rather than something proved
It holds because every triangle can be split into two right angles
questions.explanation: The standard demonstration uses a parallel line through one vertex, so alternate angles reassemble the three angles onto a straight line.

questions.stem: A circle's radius is tripled. What happens to its circumference?
options: It becomes nine times as large
questions.explanation: Circumference is directly proportional to radius. Area, not circumference, would scale by nine.

questions.stem: What is the perimeter of a rectangle 6 cm by 4 cm?
questions.explanation: Perimeter is 2 × (6 + 4) = 20. The answer 24 is the area.
questions.teaching:
Perimeter is the total distance around the outside of a shape, so it is found by adding the side lengths.

For a rectangle there are two pairs of equal sides, so add a length and a width and double the result. For a square all four sides are equal, so multiply one side by four. The units stay as lengths — centimetres, not square centimetres — which is the quickest check that you have calculated perimeter rather than area. Confusing the two is the most common error in this topic.

questions.stem: How many degrees are in a straight angle?
questions.explanation: A straight angle is half a full turn.
questions.teaching:
Angles have standard names based on their size, and the key reference points are worth fixing.

A right angle is a quarter turn. An angle smaller than that is acute, and one between a right angle and a half turn is obtuse. A half turn forms a straight line, which is why angles sitting along a straight line always add to that amount — a fact used constantly in geometry problems. A full turn is twice that again, and anything between a half turn and a full turn is called reflex.

questions.stem: What is an acute angle?
questions.explanation: Acute angles are sharp. Between 90 and 180 is obtuse.

questions.stem: What is an obtuse angle?
questions.explanation: Obtuse angles are wider than a right angle but less than a straight one.

questions.stem: What is the radius of a circle?
options: The distance from the centre to the edge
The distance across the whole circle
questions.explanation: The diameter is twice the radius, and the circumference is the distance around.

questions.stem: How many millimetres are in a centimetre?
questions.explanation: Ten millimetres make one centimetre.
questions.teaching:
Metric conversions all run on prefixes, so learning the prefixes once covers every unit instead of memorising each pair separately.

'Milli' means a thousandth, 'centi' a hundredth, and 'kilo' a thousand. That holds whether the base unit is the metre, the gram or the litre, which is why the same numbers keep reappearing. To convert, ask whether you are moving to a larger unit or a smaller one: to a smaller unit the number gets bigger, and to a larger unit it gets smaller. Checking the direction before doing the arithmetic catches most mistakes.

questions.stem: How many centimetres are in a metre?
questions.explanation: One hundred centimetres make a metre.
questions.teaching:
Metric prefixes are consistent, so learning them once covers every unit rather than each conversion separately.

"Milli" means a thousandth, "centi" means a hundredth, and "kilo" means a thousand. That is true whether you are dealing with metres, grams or litres. So the relationship asked about here follows straight from the prefix, and the near-miss option — a thousand — is the millimetre relationship instead. The word "century" shares the same root, which is a useful hook. Getting these right matters because unit errors are among the most common ways an otherwise correct calculation goes wrong.

questions.stem: What is the area of a triangle with base 8 cm and height 5 cm?
questions.explanation: Half of 8 × 5 gives 20. Forgetting the half gives 40.

questions.stem: What is the volume of a cube with side 3 cm?
questions.explanation: Three cubed is 3 × 3 × 3 = 27.

questions.stem: A rectangle has area 60 cm^2 and length 12 cm. What is its width?
questions.explanation: Dividing area by length gives the width.

questions.stem: Two angles on a straight line: one is 115 degrees. What is the other?
questions.explanation: They must total 180, so 180 - 115 = 65.

questions.stem: A triangle has two angles of 40 degrees each. What is the third?
questions.explanation: 180 - 80 = 100. This triangle is isosceles and obtuse.

questions.stem: Parallel lines are crossed by a transversal. One alternate angle is 72 degrees. What is the other?
questions.explanation: Alternate angles are equal when the lines are parallel.

questions.stem: A circle has radius 7 cm. Using pi = 22/7, what is the circumference?
questions.explanation: Circumference is 2 × 22/7 × 7 = 44. The value 154 would be the area.

questions.stem: What is the volume of a prism with cross-section 25 cm^2 and length 8 cm?
questions.explanation: Cross-sectional area multiplied by length.

questions.stem: A parallelogram has base 9 cm and height 4 cm. What is its area?
questions.explanation: Base times perpendicular height, with no halving.

questions.stem: Why does a triangle's area formula halve the rectangle's?
options: A triangle is exactly half of the rectangle with the same base and height
questions.explanation: Two identical triangles fit together to make the enclosing rectangle.

questions.stem: The interior angles of a hexagon total how many degrees?
questions.explanation: A hexagon splits into four triangles, so 4 × 180 = 720.

questions.stem: A cube's surface area is made of how many identical square faces?
questions.explanation: Six faces, which is why surface area is 6 times one face's area.

questions.stem: A rectangle's length is doubled and its width halved. What happens to its area?
questions.explanation: The two changes cancel: 2 × 1/2 = 1.

questions.stem: Why can two rectangles have the same perimeter but different areas?
options: Area and perimeter are always equal
Perimeter constrains the total of the sides, not how they are distributed
The longer rectangle must always have the greater area
questions.explanation: A 1 by 9 and a 5 by 5 rectangle both have perimeter 20 but areas of 9 and 25.

questions.stem: Which rectangle with perimeter 20 cm has the largest area?
questions.explanation: For a fixed perimeter, the square gives the maximum area.

questions.stem: A circle's radius is doubled. What happens to its area?
options: It becomes eight times as large
It becomes four times as large
questions.explanation: Area depends on the radius squared, so doubling multiplies it by four.

questions.stem: A tank is 1 m by 0.5 m by 0.4 m. How many litres does it hold?
questions.explanation: Volume is 0.2 cubic metres, and one cubic metre is 1000 litres.

questions.stem: Why is perpendicular height used rather than slant height for a parallelogram's area?
options: Slant height gives a smaller answer
Area depends on the true separation of the parallel sides
The slant height is easier to measure
questions.explanation: Using the longer slant side would overstate the area.

questions.stem: What is the perimeter of a square with side 9 cm?
questions.explanation: Four equal sides, so 4 × 9 = 36. The value 81 is the area.

questions.explanation: The prefix kilo means one thousand.

questions.explanation: One litre is one thousand millilitres.

questions.stem: What is the diameter of a circle with radius 12 cm?
questions.explanation: The diameter runs right across the circle through the centre, so it is twice the radius. Halving instead of doubling gives the radius back.

questions.stem: What is the area of a rectangle 15 cm by 2 cm?
questions.explanation: Multiply length by width. The value 34 is the perimeter.

questions.stem: How many square centimetres are in a square metre?
questions.explanation: A metre is 100 cm, and area scales with the square: 100 × 100.

questions.stem: What is the volume of a rectangular prism 5 cm by 5 cm by 2 cm?
questions.explanation: Multiply all three dimensions together.

questions.stem: What instrument measures angles?
questions.explanation: Protractors are marked in degrees.

questions.stem: What is the sum of angles around a point?
questions.explanation: Angles around a point make a full turn.

questions.stem: What is the height used in the area formula for a triangle?
options: The perpendicular height from the base
questions.explanation: It must be at right angles to the base.

questions.stem: A square has area 144 cm^2. What is its side length?
questions.explanation: A square's area is side x side, so the side is the square root: 12 x 12 = 144. Halving the area instead gives 72, which is the common error.

questions.stem: A triangle has area 30 cm^2 and height 10 cm. What is its base?
questions.explanation: Area is half base times height, so 30 = 5 × base, giving base = 6.

questions.stem: Two angles are complementary and one is 37 degrees. What is the other?
questions.explanation: Complementary angles total 90 degrees, so 90 - 37 = 53. Supplementary angles are the pair that total 180, which is the usual confusion.

questions.stem: A circle has diameter 21 cm. Using pi = 22/7, what is the circumference?
questions.explanation: Circumference is pi times diameter, so 22/7 × 21 = 66 cm.

questions.stem: A cube has edge 5 cm. What is its total surface area?
questions.explanation: Six faces of 25 cm^2 each. The value 125 is the volume.

questions.stem: The interior angles of a heptagon total how many degrees?
questions.explanation: A seven-sided polygon splits into five triangles, so 5 × 180 = 900.

questions.stem: Parallel lines crossed by a transversal give a corresponding angle of 118 degrees. What is its pair?
questions.explanation: Corresponding angles are equal between parallel lines.

questions.stem: A prism has a trapezium cross-section of area 18 cm^2 and length 7 cm. What is its volume?
questions.explanation: Volume of any right prism is cross-sectional area times length.

questions.stem: Why is 1 cubic metre equal to 1000 litres?
options: A litre is a cubic metre
A cubic metre is 1 000 000 cubic centimetres and each litre is 1000 of those
A litre is defined as one thousandth of any volume
questions.explanation: Working through the unit conversion shows where the factor comes from.

questions.stem: A rectangle and a triangle have the same base and height. How do their areas compare?
options: The triangle's area is half the rectangle's
questions.explanation: The halving factor in the triangle formula reflects exactly this relationship.

questions.stem: Why does doubling every dimension of a cube multiply its surface area by four but its volume by eight?
options: Area depends on two dimensions and volume on three
Surface area and volume scale identically
questions.explanation: This square-cube relationship explains why large animals need proportionally thicker legs.

questions.stem: A circular pond has radius 3 m. Approximately how much fencing is needed to surround it?
questions.explanation: Circumference is 2 × pi × 3, roughly 18.8 m.

questions.stem: Why must the height in a parallelogram's area formula be measured perpendicular to the base?
options: Only the perpendicular distance gives the true separation of the parallel sides
It is a convention with no reason
The slant height gives the same answer
questions.explanation: Using the sloping side would overstate the area, sometimes considerably.

questions.stem: Two triangles have the same area but different shapes. What must be true?
options: Their base and height products are equal
questions.explanation: Many different base and height combinations give the same product.

questions.stem: A rectangle is 6 cm wide and 14 cm tall. What is its area, in square centimetres?
questions.explanation: Area of a rectangle is width x height, so 6 x 14 = 84 cm². Area is measured in square units because you are covering a surface, not walking around it. The classic error is finding the perimeter instead — that would be 2 x (6 + 14) = 40 cm, which answers a different question.

questions.stem: A rectangle is 4 cm wide and 14 cm tall. What is its area, in square centimetres?
questions.explanation: Area of a rectangle is width x height, so 4 x 14 = 56 cm². Area is measured in square units because you are covering a surface, not walking around it. The classic error is finding the perimeter instead — that would be 2 x (4 + 14) = 36 cm, which answers a different question.

questions.stem: A triangle has a base of 4 cm and a perpendicular height of 3 cm. What is its area, in square centimetres?
questions.explanation: Area of a triangle is half the base times the height: (4 x 3) / 2 = 6 cm². The halving is the whole point — any triangle is exactly half of the rectangle that encloses it on the same base and height. Forgetting to halve gives 12 cm², which is the commonest wrong answer here.

questions.stem: A triangle has a base of 16 cm and a perpendicular height of 7 cm. What is its area, in square centimetres?
questions.explanation: Area of a triangle is half the base times the height: (16 x 7) / 2 = 56 cm². The halving is the whole point — any triangle is exactly half of the rectangle that encloses it on the same base and height. Forgetting to halve gives 112 cm², which is the commonest wrong answer here.

questions.stem: A triangle has a base of 4 cm and a perpendicular height of 5 cm. What is its area, in square centimetres?
questions.explanation: Area of a triangle is half the base times the height: (4 x 5) / 2 = 10 cm².
